titel: Sugar, salt and alcohol lower the freezing point
kurz: Dissolved sugar, salt or alcohol get in the way of water as it freezes. It only freezes at lower temperatures, and part of it stays liquid.
bild_im_kopf: Like a dance floor full of people: the more strangers standing in between, the harder it is for the couples to find each other.
was_passiert: Water molecules have to line up in a lattice to freeze. Dissolved particles get in the way, so the solution only freezes below 0 °C. In ice cream, part always stays liquid, so it stays scoopable. The other way round, [[salz|salt]] melts ice: ice with salt turns into a brine that can get as cold as about minus 21 °C.
warum_wichtig: Explains why low-[[zucker|sugar]] ice cream turns rock hard, why a splash of alcohol keeps sorbet soft and how to make ice cream in a bag with ice and salt.
synonyme: why ice cream does not go hard
faustregeln: Ice cream and sorbet need enough sugar, otherwise they turn hard.
A tablespoon of spirits keeps sorbet softer; too much stops it from freezing.
Ice with salt chills faster and deeper than ice alone.

praxis.text: Sorbet made from very sweet fruit turns out softer by itself than one made from lemon.

skala.name: ice with salt: this cold the brine can get
